newsitem.title: USA: Argentina's Fernandez sees no bond deal increase.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez sees no bond deal increase.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernndez said Friday that the country has no plans to increase the global bond deal announced this morning.
The Argentine economy ministry said Friday it would issue $750 million of dollar-denominated 10-year bonds via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers to take advantage of favorable market conditions.
"For the time being, we have only the $750 million issue," Fernndez said at a press conference here. "Later, we will see... These things are permanently under study."

Fernndez also said the country has no immediate plans to buy back any of its outstanding Brady bonds, but said the economy ministry would continue to study the matter as part of its 1996 funding operation.
Turning to the general strike underway in Argentina, Fernndez said the country needed to introduce greater flexibility into its labor markets and blamed labor union leaders for the protests.
"The strike does not accomplish anything," he said. "We have to introduce more flexibility to have more competitive labor markets."
Fernndez applauded the congressional approval of his tax package, which would narrow the country's fiscal deficit.
Since Congress changed the measures only slightly, Argentina would not need to modify its letter of intent to the International Monetary Fund, Fernndez said.
Fernndez said he could not comment on spread talk for the new bond.

Argentine Undersecretary of Financing Miguel Kiguel said the ministry was attempting to price the issue so that it would trade higher when it leaves the primary market, as opposed to previous Argentine global bond deals.
